outcome: No result addressing whether a first-order theory with minimum universality spectrum exists was found in the window; the only substantive Shelah paper on this exact question (SH1164, 'Universality; new criterion for non-existence') predates the frozen revision by over two years.
summary: The universality spectrum problem asks whether some complete first-order theory has a minimum universality spectrum among all such theories (a theory Tceq — an equivalence relation with a family of choice functions — is the leading candidate believed to be minimal or near-minimal among non-simple theories). The last substantive contribution I could find is Shelah's SH1164, 'Universality: new criterion for non-existence,' posted to arXiv as 2108.06727 on 2021-08-15 (v2: 2022-03-14) and published in Bollettino dell'Unione Matematica Italiana in 2023 — this gives new sufficient conditions for non-existence of universal models for Tceq at various cardinals, but does not settle the minimality question and predates the frozen revision (26 January 2024) regardless. I searched broadly for any 2024-2026 work continuing this line — direct searches on 'universality spectrum,' searches for Shelah's more recent papers, and searches for the specific candidate theory Tceq/Tfeq — and found nothing addressing the stated question. I did find two adjacent but distinct 2025 papers, 'On the spectrum of limit models' (Beard & Mazari-Armida, arXiv:2503.11605) and 'The spectrum of limit models in a first order setting' (Beard, arXiv:2510.03459); I opened the abstract/content of the first and confirmed by direct inspection that it concerns the isomorphism spectrum of limit models in abstract elementary classes (a different, though terminologically similar, question about when limit models are isomorphic to each other) rather than the existence of universal models or the universality spectrum ordering of theories. This is a related-problem/different-question case under §3.1, not a case of the stated problem, so it does not count. I was unable to fully render Shelah's SH1164 PDF as text via the fetch tool (it returned raw PDF markup), but I independently confirmed its arXiv posting date and abstract content through the arXiv abstract page and a published-journal citation, which is sufficient to establish it predates the window. No AI system appears anywhere in any of the sources found. This agrees with the triage's 'none' verdict; I did not find its dismissal of the Tceq/limit-model adjacent work to be wrong.
competing_reading: If the Beard–Mazari-Armida 'spectrum of limit models' line were judged to be close enough in substance to the universality spectrum (both concern classifying models of a theory by an ordering related to embeddability/isomorphism across cardinals), one could argue it deserves a 'partial'/'progress' classification with a caveat. I do not think this is the better reading: the universality spectrum problem specifically concerns universal (embedding) models, and the limit-model spectrum concerns isomorphism types of models built by increasing chains — these are different mathematical objects studied with different techniques (types/independence relations vs. combinatorial non-embeddability arguments), and neither paper mentions universal models or Shelah's SH1164 line of work in what I reviewed.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that either exhibits a first-order theory provably minimum in the universality spectrum ordering, proves no such minimum exists, or narrows the class of candidate minimal theories (e.g. further sufficient/necessary conditions for Tceq or Tfeq specifically) would settle or advance this. Direct access to Shelah's personal publication list (shelah.logic.at) with working links, which returned a 404 for the listing page I tried, could also surface a newer unlisted preprint if one exists.
